comments.story: Mourning and moving on: rituals for leaving a career (2014)
comments.text: There was a lengthy interview with Peter Thiel a few years back: [VIDEO] It's interesting and worth watching, but it becomes apparent that Thiel is a financier, and science takes place on a different timescale. Better seek advice from someone who was active when US science was still functional, let's say Roy Vagelos.

I've studied Thiel, he's just not mainstream left. If you want to listen to him with good faith, I enjoyed this interview: [VIDEO] Doesn't come across evil to me unless by evil you mean just not mainstream left, which might be the correct in the valley.

comments.story: Ask HN: What were your most impactful podcast episodes from 2019?
comments.text: The first episode of "the portal" was great. In that episode Eric Weinstein and Peter Thiel deeply discussed a variety of topics. [VIDEO]

> the visceral reaction against FLoC The article title contains the word "everybody" which is evidence of the authors tendency to deal in absolutes. He is claiming to speak for us all with this loose assimilation of words ("hates" further describes an emotional disposition towards idea proposal, and the tagline is equally charming). Let's make it our mission to be polite for a cleaner archive of Internet Interaction Instances. I will not match the negative energy and instead proceed to be cordial&calculated in the delivery of my opinion (I lost sleep over this last night). Thiel on Weinstein's "Portal" ventured the "eye of Sauron" metaphor [0] to describe the effect of surveillance on generations developing during the Information Age. The "double-slit experiment" is also relevant here (modern scientific lore suggesting that the act of observation influences outcome - "spooky action").…
